text: Stand on salt for ten minutes and watch what happens to your body. Spread a thick layer on the floor, step on it barefoot, and just stand still. Feel the coarse grains press into your soles.

The soles of your feet are among the most sensitive parts of your body, thousands of nerve endings waking at once. Your attention drops out of your racing head and into your feet. Your shoulders soften. Your breath slows.
Tension you did not know you were holding begins to release. And that night, you may sleep deeper than you have in years. In our monastery, salt was never just for food.

The monks use it in purification practices, to mark a boundary between what the day gathered and what the night deserves. Ten quiet minutes. That is the whole practice. The salt brings you back into your body.
Keeping the calm once you step off, that is the deeper art. Everything I know is inside The Quiet Between Thoughts. The link is in my profile.
